sentences.text: ?Court No. - 1
Case :- Criminal Misc. Writ Petition No. - 1382 of 2023

Petitioner :- Bhagvan Deen Chaudhary
Respondent :- State Of U.P. Thru. Prin. Secy. Home. Lko And Others
Counsel for Petitioner :- Farooq Ayoob

Counsel for Respondent :- G.A.
Hon'ble Ramesh Sinha,J.
Hon'ble Narendra Kumar Johari,J.

Heard Shri Farooq Ayoob, learned Counsel for the petitioner, Shri S.N. Tilahari, learned Additional Government Advocate for the State-respondents no.1, 2 and 3 and perused the impugned F.I.R. as well as material brought on record.
It has been argued by learned Counsel for the petitioner that the petitioner is a practicing Advocate and he is not named in the FIR.
He further submits that petitioner has neither signed in any document nor any signature belongs to him.

The date of incident has also not been mentioned in the FIR, which has been lodged after an inordinate delay on 14.01.2023 without any plausible Bhagvan Deen Chaudhary vs State Of U.P. Thru. Prin. Secy. Home. Lko ... on 21 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/92959951/

sentences.text: He further submits that the petitioner has criminal history of one case, i.e. FIR No.0442 of 2023, under Sections 419, 420, 467, 468, 471, 406 I.P.C. against which he has preferred Criminal Misc. Writ Petition No.209 of 2023 before this Court, in which interim protection has been granted.

entities.text: Criminal Misc. Writ Petition No.209 of 2023
entities.label: CASE_NUMBER

sentences.text: He next argued that the dispute is of purely civil in nature and the petitioner is being harassed by the police in pursuance of the impugned FIR.
Learned Additional Government Advocate, on the other hand, opposed the prayer for quashing of the F.I.R. and argued that the name of the petitioner came into light during investigation.
The complainant is the Branch Manager of Aryavat Gramin Bank, Ram Nagar.
From a perusal of FIR, it transpires that some villagers, named in the FIR, had taken loan from the Bank on the basis of false Gata number.

He further submits that the petitioner in connivance with the co-accused persons committed fraud with the Bank by providing loan on the basis of false gata numbers, hence the writ petition is liable to be dismissed.

After having examined the submissions advanced by learned Counsel for the parties and considering the fact that the name of the petitioner has come into light during investigation and he in connivance with co-accused committed fraud with the bank by providing loan on the basis of false documents, hence, no interference is called for by this Court in its extraordinary power under Article 226 of the Constitution of India for quashing of the FIR or for grant of any interim relief to the petitioner.

The petition lacks merit and is, accordingly, dismissed.
.
(Narendra Kumar Johari, J.) (Ramesh Sinha, J.) Order Date :- 21.2.2023
Anand Sri./-
